page: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The server runs on a KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance characteristics across multiple domains. In CPU testing, the instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 63,623.58 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 98,466.88, both placing in the top 25 percent. Memory performance is highly competitive, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 4,744.5 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 135.71 GB/sec. Database operations are a notable strength, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 30,782.6 and a Redis SET throughput of 75.95 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performed in the top 25 percent at 432.71 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression and static web serving throughput fell into the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r3-256 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading, ensuring predictable, dedicated CPU performance. Given the high memory capacity, strong database benchmark results, and fast local NVMe storage, this server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
